name: Malkavian Society: The Madness Network and Clan Practices

text.content:
Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} has no single name for its shared, disembodied psychic connection — the clan simply calls it "the connection," since the connection is the clan, the clan is Malkav, and Malkav is the connection. Outsiders and different circles within the family use a dozen different names for the same phenomenon: the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Madness Network, the Cobweb, the Tapestry, the weavery, Metatron, the Mouth of God, or the nerves of Malkav. Whatever it is called, it is treated as canon clan lore rather than mere metaphor: a supernatural, disembodied neural net linking (to varying degree) every member of the clan.

The Network is not constant telepathic chatter. Most Malkavians hear only a faint flutter of voices a few times a year, more often as a clan gathering approaches; the vast majority of a Lunatic's nights are spent alone with nothing in her skull but her own dementia. Some clan members are far more sensitive than others for reasons nobody has ever proven — a given cousin might get a flutter once a week, while another can barely be raised even by physically fetching her.

The precise nature and origin of the Network is deliberately left unresolved, even in clan legend. Popular theories include: that Malkav's own consciousness persists, distributed across the minds of his descendants; that Malkav built the Network deliberately as a means of watching the world through his childer's eyes even in his sleep; that it is a blood-transmitted sympathetic link analogous to (but distinct from) the blood bond, since it does not affect @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} ghouls; or that it is a form of racial memory so advanced that some Malkavians perceive events as they happen elsewhere. No theory is confirmed, and the clan's Antediluvian is not available for comment. Storytellers should treat the Network as fully theirs to define and use (or ignore) as suits the chronicle — it is a vehicle for plot hooks and revelations, not a fixed system.

Access and immunity: The Cobweb is not a function of the Dementation Discipline itself — a non-Malkavian who learns Dementation can never hear the Call or tap the Network. Conversely, any vampire with at least one dot of the Malkavian Time Talent (see below) is, by clan definition, a Malkavian, connected to the clan's Disciplines and communication network whether or not her sire stuck around to teach her anything.

Malkavian-sired @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.SNuXttNqxzJ6uPXv]{Caitiff}: Not every childe of a Malkavian is Malkavian. Sires who Embrace someone who winds up sane, or who abandon a childe immediately after the Embrace, produce @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.SNuXttNqxzJ6uPXv]{Caitiff}. Such a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.SNuXttNqxzJ6uPXv]{Caitiff} may or may not inherit a derangement (the player's choice, or the Storyteller's, per the Storyteller's preference) but never develops the clan's Disciplines or a clan connection on her own. If a Storyteller wishes to allow a Malkavian-sired Caitiff partial access to the Madness Network, that Caitiff must have a derangement and cannot purchase dots of Malkavian Time (treat her as using Wits alone in the relevant pool). By and large, the clan does not tolerate eavesdroppers: a Caitiff demonstrating a connection to the Network is hunted down and destroyed on principle.

Wherever more than a handful of Malkavians share a city, the clan periodically convenes a gathering: an informal clan meeting called by whichever cousin feels moved (or has business enough) to call one. Attendance is a strong point of etiquette within the family, since the summons — called the Call — is felt by every clan member in range as an escalating psychic pressure. A Call heard faintly a week out from a thousand miles away grows louder as the gathering nears, and can become a continuous, distracting whisper for any @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} physically present in the host city while the gathering is underway.

Not every clan member perceives the Call equally: some can shrug it off entirely, while others must be forcibly retrieved when a gathering approaches, apparently unable to sense it at all. Gatherings serve no fixed purpose — some are purely social, some exist to coordinate a "crusade" (a shared clan project such as tormenting a hostile prince or unsettling a community of mortals), and some seem to exist only to give a handful of elders cover to conduct their own business in front of the rest of the family without anyone quite noticing. Other clans are technically permitted to observe a gathering out of professional curiosity, but Malkavians are rarely comfortable with outside eyes on family business.

Pranking is one of clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian}'s most consistent cultural institutions, though it is widely misunderstood by outsiders. Contrary to popular belief, pranking is not primarily about gaining status among peers — there is no guarantee a brilliant prank earns its architect any regard at all. It is better understood as part compulsion, part intellectual exercise, and part an act of sharing: the prankster is trying to give the target a taste of seeing the world as a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} sees it, cracks and all.

Any vampire who is a rigid creature of habit — hunting the same three clubs every Friday, say — is considered fair (even deserving) game. A fellow Lunatic whose own derangement already makes him a stickler for order is generally spared, on the reasoning that he already perceives "something other than the cave walls" and a prank would be redundant. The most extreme form of pranking, sometimes whispered of as "reality busting," targets an entire clan or a Storyteller-sanctioned significant target with an elaborate, sustained, multi-city campaign of induced doubt, hallucination and stage-managed "gatherings" designed to make the victim question his own sanity in the buildup to an Embrace or as an act of collective clan theater.

Pranking Malkavians receive no formal diplomatic immunity for the practice. There is an unspoken understanding between @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} elders and the elders of other clans that only so much "levity" will be tolerated; if a prank crosses a line and its target retaliates, the rest of the clan generally will not lift a finger to protect the prankster. The shrewdest Lunatics know when to stop.

Unlike most clans, Malkavians hold no single agreed tradition or philosophy — the clan itself insists it needs none. What outsiders sometimes mistake for organized "clan traditions" are really a loose, ever-shifting set of personal and small-group philosophies that individual Malkavians drift toward, argue over, and abandon. None of these are formal institutions with membership rolls or hierarchy; they are useful shorthand for Storytellers describing the range of belief found across the clan:

  • Illumination: A drive to teach, to force open the doors of others' minds whether they want it or not — pranking taken to an evangelical extreme.
  • Iconoclasm: A compulsion to shatter others' sacred cows and treasured certainties, forcing them to sift the wreckage for what actually matters.
  • Detachment: A philosophy of using material goods and relationships without ever being owned by them, on the theory that transcendence is impossible while shackled to things, living or dead.
  • Divine Connection: The conviction that one's madness is a personal link to something sublime or holy, common among clan members Embraced in eras when "possession" was the only available vocabulary for mental illness.
  • Ignorance/Zen Psychosis: A rejection of thought and rationality altogether in favor of pure reflexive action — "Malkavians on autopilot," without guilt, shame, or choice, because reflexes cannot be judged.
  • Nihilism: A terminal breakdown of all of the above, embraced most often by those (young and old alike) who sense Gehenna approaching and give themselves over to its finality.

The "antitribu" (@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}) wing of the clan overlays its own justification on top of these currents: that the sacred duty of every true child of Malkav is to spread his blood and "infection" as thinly and widely as possible, fracturing their god-sire's dormant essence into pieces too small and numerous for him ever to reassemble and wake in full — a duty the antitribu claim the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} side of the family shares without admitting it, since the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} likewise replaces every madman it destroys with two new @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} childer.

Not every @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Embrace produces a functional (if mad) vampire. A rare, whispered-about failure state exists within the clan: childer who come through the Embrace catastrophically broken, reduced to shrieking, physically superhuman, utterly non-functional wrecks, sometimes called the Gnawed ("nothing left but bones"). Clan elders reportedly recognize the condition on sight and treat it as a matter for immediate, quiet handling: the Gnawed are removed from circulation, and rumor holds that at least some are kept somewhere — not destroyed outright — in what younger clan members imagine as pits or asylum-like holding cells, possibly as feeding stock or hostages of unknown purpose for older generations. Nothing about the Gnawed is confirmed clan lore even inside the family; it exists as a horror-flavored plot hook and cautionary rumor for Storytellers to use (or not) as a chronicle demands, not as a defined game mechanic.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Time is a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian}-exclusive Talent representing a Lunatic's particular sensitivity to the clan's shared subconscious, letting her "plug into" the Madness Network and filter its floodwaters into something at least marginally useful. It cannot be purchased by any vampire outside clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian}, and has no specialties.

Sensing gatherings: A Malkavian need not have any dots in this Talent at all to involuntarily receive the Call or other broadcasts along the Network — in fact, newly Embraced clan members with no dots at all are often driven especially mad by messages arriving with no context. Dots in Malkavian Time instead govern how much useful warning a character gets ahead of a significant gathering: at the Storyteller's discretion, roughly a week of advance notice yields a vague locational impulse only once the gathering has already begun, growing clearer and earlier with a stronger connection, up to a full week's warning and a clear sense of the gathering's purpose for the most sensitive Lunatics. Tapping too deeply carries a real risk: an unusually strong pull can mean the character is picking up bleed-through from her elders' derangements rather than useful information.

Death-sense: A sufficiently attuned Malkavian (three or more dots of Malkavian Time in the Trait-rating source material) can sense a clanmate's death-scream over the Network, so long as it occurs within the same city. Beyond this, the Network is not a substitute for a phone: sending a deliberate, personalized message to a specific person along the Cobweb is very difficult even for a talented Lunatic, requires real effort, and can only carry a couple of words per success on the attempt.

MET note: Malkavian Time is a Storyteller-mediated Trait rather than something a player resolves alone at the table — use it to seed advance notice of clan gatherings, deliver cryptic warnings, or convey a clanmate's death off-scene, calibrating detail and lead time to how invested the character is in the Network.

pages.name: The Sight and Reputation as Seers

text.content: Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian}'s reputation for prophecy and oracular insight (sometimes called simply "the Sight" within the family) is treated as older and more grounded in fact than the clan's reputation for pure insanity, though the two are entangled in outsiders' minds. Elders in particular, after centuries of living with the Sight and the Network without the benefit of modern psychiatric vocabulary, are prone to interpreting their own visions as communion with the divine. Younger clan members are more likely to frame the same phenomena in clinical or skeptical terms, while suspecting — without proof — that some family members deliberately encourage the "seer" reputation as a long-running prank on credulous outsiders, or that some @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} foretellings are the product of unusually patient, long-term surveillance rather than genuine precognition. No formal Discipline power is required to produce this reputation; it exists as clan color and Storyteller-facing flavor to justify why other clans and factions sometimes seek out a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian}'s counsel despite (or because of) the family's madness.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Malkavian, Chapter Two - Inside Bedlam
